findings.reason: a coordinator following the followup would dispatch §2 in parallel and it would import a helper that does not yet exist, failing on the node that most depends on the ordering.
findings.text: the followup body says "§1 and §2 dispatch in parallel", contradicting the declared dependency `plan-section-depends-on` `s2:["a-landing-reads-binary-files#s1"]` (snapshot line 29) and §2's own Sequence ("§2 runs after §1 lands and imports those helpers"), because §2's done-when imports `_write_origin_and_checkout` and `_complete_land` from `tests/helpers/landing_repository.py`, which §1's write paths are what create

findings.reason: a test written literally against `land_merge` passes on the unfixed code, so the node's central measure would be a suite that passes before the repair.
findings.text: §1's first done-when bullet asserts "`merge.land_merge` lands that head without raising", but `land_merge` (`reckon/crew/merge.py:474`) reads no blob content — no `_show`, no `git show`, no content diff — so it cannot raise the `UnicodeDecodeError` the section's negative control requires, and its report carries no `survived` block (that block is produced only by `land()` at `reckon/crew/merge.py:652`), which the next bullet asserts

findings.reason: the mechanism claim (rev-parse yields a blob id without decoding) is true and the primary anchor resolves, so only a reader re-checking that one pointer is misled.
findings.text: §1's "Why" says the module "already resolves object names this way (near lines 125 and 264)", but in `reckon/crew/merge.py` the `rev-parse` calls are at lines 125, 133 and 345; line 264 is inside the `change_markers` docstring and resolves nothing, so the second half of that citation is stale

findings.reason: collapsing all five into one refusal function would regress the exit-6 push-outstanding contract and the non-fatal release-error path, both of which the plan's own gate tests assert, so the worker must be told which sites are refusals and which are not.
findings.text: §2 claims a single merge-failure-to-refusal mapping (type, message, resume command, exit status) "is written out at five sites … near lines 2449, 2475, 2485 and 2524" and that "all five call the new function, and none keeps a catch of its own", but of those four sites `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:2475` catches `MergePushOutstandingError` — a landing whose push is outstanding, reported `ok: true` with `steps.land.push_outstanding` and exit `PUSH_OUTSTANDING_EXIT` (6), pinned by `tests/test_a_reviewed_head_lands_without_touching_the_index.py:352` — and `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:2524` catches a `_rev_parse` failure inside the release, recorded under `steps.release.push_error` rather than as a land refusal

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — the §1 "Why" cites "near lines 125 and 264" as places `reckon/crew/merge.py` resolves object names; line 125 does, line 264 carries no `rev-parse` call.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §1's done-when asserts `merge.land_merge` lands the binary head, but the marker check under test lives in `merge.land`, so the named entry point cannot raise the failure the section's own negative control requires.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both gate logs are stated to live under the run directory (a durable crew path), and the evidence fragments are written under `docs/evidence/fragments/<slug>/` in the repository, not a scratchpad or node-local temp.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test modules (`test_a_landing_reads_binary_files.py`, `test_a_failed_land_exits_nonzero.py`), the shared helper (`tests/helpers/landing_repository.py`) and the report key `blob_identity` are named by mechanism; no plan label, stage name, ticket number or changelog prose reaches a symbol or path.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §2 asserts that one merge-failure-to-refusal mapping is written out at five caller sites and that "none keeps a catch of its own", but two of the four promoted-land sites it names are not that mapping.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §1 carries the blob-aware landing check alone, §2 carries "a failure after promotion reports itself" alone; §2's extraction of the shared refusal function is the means to that one goal, not a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — the plan declares `plan-section-depends-on` `s2 -> s1` and §2's Sequence restates that order, but the plan's only open followup (`f-alrbf-001`) tells a coordinator to dispatch "§1 and §2 … in parallel".
